== Adnex-bound pro-sumti and '''zo'au''' ==

;'''zo'au''' {{selmaho|KOhA}} : begin postnex
* Every '''zo'au''' corresponds to an implicit or explicit '''zo'u''' in the same bridi. '''zo'u--zo'au''' correspondences nest. Every implicit or explicit '''zo'u''' terminates a prenex. Every '''zo'au''' begins a postnex. A postnex and its matching prenex jointly form an adnex. Scope of elements within the same adnex is left-to-right: the earlier element has scope over the later. Items in an outer adnex have scope over every item in an inner adnex.

;'''koi'a''' {{selmaho|KOhA}} : adnex-bound pro-sumti

;'''koi'e''' {{selmaho|KOhA}} : adnex-bound pro-sumti

;'''foi'o''' {{selmaho|KOhA}} : adnex-bound pro-sumti

;'''foi'u''' {{selmaho|KOhA}} : adnex-bound pro-sumti
* Binding of adnex-bound pro-sumti in a prenex. The nth adnex-bound pro-sumti in a prenex is bound by the nth adnex-bound pro-sumti in the postnex portion of the same adnex.
* Binding of adnex-bound pro-sumti, A, that is not in a prenex:
** If there is another adnex-bound pro-sumti, P, in a prenex with scope over A, and P and A have the same shape, then P binds A.
** Otherwise, A is bound by sumti S (as if S were '''S goi A'''), where S is the leftmost sumti satisfying the following conditions:
*** S is in an adnex with scope over A.
*** S is not a quantified da-series KOhA.
*** S does not already contain a '''goi KOhA'''.
*** S does not already bind an earlier adnex-bound pro-sumti.
* I think the above requires a better explanation, as it sounds like it could be useful - but everything below here seems like frivolous ways to save syllables. It is not a flaw in Lojban if sentences happen to be longer than their English equivalents! --{{selmaho|rab.spir}}
* It is a flaw in Lojban if we shun the precision it affords us just because the precision requires too much verbosity. There is no implicit comparison to English; English is incapable of the precision, fullstop. --{{selmaho|User:And Rosta}}
